title: Representation learning uncovers the extragalactic X-ray transient XRT 200515 in Chandra archives
summary: A representation-learning pipeline searched archived Chandra event data and identified XRT 200515, a previously unnoticed extragalactic fast X-ray transient in the Large Magellanic Cloud. Its light curve has a sharp sub-10-second hard burst followed by an approximately 800-second oscillating tail with spectral softening. The paper discusses possible origins including a low-energy giant magnetar flare or a Type I burst from a faint low-mass X-ray binary; the source's physical nature is unresolved.
ai_technology: Unsupervised representation-learning pipeline using sparse autoencoders, dimensionality reduction and density-based clustering
organization: Stanford University; Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics; Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory; collaborators

evidence.tested: A representation-learning pipeline searched archived Chandra event data and identified XRT 200515, a previously unnoticed extragalactic fast X-ray transient in the Large Magellanic Cloud.
evidence.unknown: The transient is a real source-reported observational event, but its astrophysical progenitor remains unresolved. The study also catalogs candidate flares and dips; those catalog candidates are not counted as separately confirmed discoveries.
evidence.ai_role: Converted Chandra photon event files into time-energy representations, learned low-dimensional embeddings and clustered similar events; anomalous transient-dominated clusters surfaced XRT 200515 for subsequent human inspection and astrophysical analysis.
